ranking.reason: Meets every requirement value in voltage mode at gain 32 (Configuration 1 TC TYPE 11xx). Its guaranteed budget is ±1.51 °C against ±2 °C and needs no firmware offset calibration. It detects an open thermocouple on chip (OPEN bit, FAULT pin) and has the highest input rating here, ±45 V on T+, T- and BIAS, so round 2 protection has the least to carry toward 67.2 V. Deep stock at both vendors: JLCPCB 11,459 (03:19:06Z), Digi-Key 12,023 (02:47:35Z). The type K conversion runs in firmware, as for the ADS1220.

P2's record: meets every value, with the tightest budget, ±1.35 °C, but only after a firmware offset calibration (input offset at gain 2 to 128 has a typical figure only). Its burn-out sources must be off during the measurement (SBAS501D section 8.3.10), so open detection is a separate test step. Its inputs are rated to AVDD + 0.3 V only. The most JLCPCB stock (16,924) and less at Digi-Key (660). Below the MAX31856 for the calibration dependency and the lower input rating.

The I2C counterpart of the ADS1220. It meets every value with ±1.65 °C against ±2 °C after a firmware offset calibration before each reading, the thinnest margin of the three. Its 16 addresses are 0x40 to 0x4F (Table 14), the band of the port monitors (0x40 to 0x43) and the INA238s (0x44 and up), so P5 must find it a free address or another bus. Stocked at both vendors: JLCPCB 4,147 (03:19:05Z), Digi-Key 2,585 (03:10:09Z).
